hook: A museum of the Telugu language
hookSay: Telugudanam means the essence of being Telugu. This free online museum tells the story of the language in five halls.

beats.label: Hall 1 · Script
beats.say: In the Script hall, every Telugu letter sits on one grid. Tap a filter to see which sounds are native, and which were borrowed from Sanskrit, Persian and English.

beats.label: Hall 2 · Language
beats.say: The Language hall shows that Telugu is not a daughter of Sanskrit. It is a Dravidian language, and its closest relative is Tulu.

beats.label: Hall 3 · Literature
beats.say: Literature begins in the street: Burra Katha troupes, Oggu Katha singers, and Vemana's four-line verses against caste and greed.

beats.label: Hall 4 · Diaspora
beats.say: The Diaspora hall follows Telugus from old sea trade to the Gulf and America, where they grew from about {1,500|fifteen hundred} in {1970|nineteen seventy} to over {1.2 million|one point two million} by {2024|twenty twenty-four}.

beats.label: Hall 5 · Digital Telugu
beats.say: And Digital Telugu traces the move from broken fonts to the Telugu Wikipedia in {2003|two thousand three}, and Unicode in {2004|two thousand four}.

beats.label: Read, then explore
beats.say: Every room has a page to read and an exhibit to explore. This video only shows a glimpse. Visit the site, and try the interactive exhibits yourself.

outro: Telugudanam: the essence of being Telugu. The link is on screen.

end.title: Telugudanam
